abstract: A new surface observation can extend an object map while contradicting an earlier object assignment. Treating both updates as a single merge can join unrelated objects; keeping all earlier assignments leaves fragmented objects unresolved. We present a revision module that makes these decisions separately. Historical merges require shared-mask evidence to outweigh separate-object explanations across views, including after removal of any one observation. New measured points are assigned through local competition among object seeds supported by image masks. On two preselected KITTI-360 windows, the method improves mean building/car instance AP50:90 from 17.259 to 18.762. On four further spatial holdouts, AP rises from 20.263 to 23.171, although unconditional revision reaches 23.251. Controlled comparisons attribute the gains to protecting existing identities, consolidating selected fragments, and assigning new points locally. The results also show where conservative merge decisions suppress useful updates. A garage recording demonstrates the same revision module on LiDAR--inertial--visual mapping outputs.

title: OmniSLAM: Evidence-Authorized Revision of Persistent Object Maps
